Empirical Research Plan: The Real‐Effects of Antitakeover Statutes on Firm Behavior, 1976–1995  

------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Difference-in-Differences with staggered treatment timing, augmented with dynamic event-time leads/lags.  

Why appropriate  
• Treatment (business-combination law) is enacted at different years across states but applies only to firms incorporated in the passing state.  
• The institutional narrative indicates the laws were orthogonal to real-economic shocks facing the plants: incorporation state ≠ production state, and adoption was largely lobby-driven.  
• We observe a long pre- and post-period around each adoption, permitting validation of parallel trends and estimation of dynamic responses (event study).  

------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control  

Treatment variable  
Treat_it = 1 if firm i is incorporated in state s and year t ≥ the first effective date of s’s business-combination (or other 2nd/3rd-gen) statute; 0 otherwise.  

Control group  
• Primary: Firms incorporated in states that have not yet passed the statute in year t (“not-yet-treated”) plus firms in states that never pass during 1976-95.  
• Because plants inherit their Compustat firm-level treatment, all plants of the same firm share Treat_it.  

Timing / Event date  
Adoption year is the statute’s effective date (usually within one fiscal year of passage). Event time k = t – adoption_year_s lets us build an event-study.  

No running variable; RDD not used.  

------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  

A1. Parallel trends: Absent the statute, outcome trends of treated and control firms would have moved in parallel. Plausibility: incorporation state unrelated to operating-state macro shocks; we can test with long pre-trends.  

A2. No differential anticipation: Managers/shareholders do not change behavior materially before passage. The statutes typically passed quickly and were viewed as incremental to earlier poison pills; still testable with leads in event study.  

A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): A statute in one incorporation state does not directly affect firms incorporated elsewhere. Horizontal spillovers are unlikely because laws hinge on charter state.  

A4. No time-varying composition: Firm mortality/entry is not systematically altered in a way that biases outcomes (we can show attrition rates by treatment status).  

A5. Correct specification of staggered DiD: Use estimator robust to heterogeneous treatment effects (e.g., Callaway-Sant’Anna, Sun-Abraham) so timing heterogeneity does not bias ATT.  

------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations  

T1. Selection into incorporation state (historical path dependence but still endogenous).  
• Mitigation: Include firm fixed effects, firm-specific controls (age, size), and show results are robust after excluding Delaware-incorporated firms.  
• Use “eventual adopter” sample—only states that will pass at some point—to difference out time-invariant selection.  

T2. Other contemporaneous state-charter corporate law changes (constituency statutes, control-share laws) could coincide.  
• Mitigation: Control for an indicator for each other antitakeover statute × post, or include a cumulative “AT law index” as in prior literature.  

T3. Macroeconomic or industry shocks coinciding with adoption years.  
• Mitigation: Year × 3-digit SIC and Year × region-of-plant fixed effects, allowing differential time paths.  
• Cluster standard errors two-way (incorporation state, firm) or use Driscoll-Kraay variants.  

------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline  

```r
# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)         # fast two-way FE and clustered SE
library(did)            # Callaway-Sant’Anna
# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load merged plant–firm panel
dt <- fread("lrd_compustat_merged.csv")     # one obs = plant-year

# 2. Create treatment variables
# state_incadoptyear.csv contains adoption year by charter state
statelaw <- fread("state_adoption_year.csv")   # columns: state_inc, adopt_year
dt <- merge(dt, statelaw, by = "state_inc", all.x = TRUE)

dt[, treat := ifelse(!is.na(adopt_year) & year >= adopt_year, 1L, 0L)]
dt[, event_time := ifelse(!is.na(adopt_year), year - adopt_year, NA_integer_)]

# 3. Core outcome examples
# log wage per production worker
dt[, lwage := log(wage_bill / employment)]

# 4. Main two-way FE DiD (Goodman-Bacon not biased; still use SA correction)
feols_main <- feols(lwage ~ treat | plant_id + year, data = dt,
                    cluster = ~state_inc + firm_id)
summary(feols_main)

# 5. Dynamic event-study (Sun-Abraham)
es <- feols(lwage ~ sunab(adopt_year, year) | plant_id + year,
            data = dt, cluster = ~state_inc + firm_id)
iplot(es, ref.line = 0, xlab = "Years relative to adoption")

# 6. Alternative estimator – Callaway-Sant’Anna ATT
cs <- att_gt(yname = "lwage",
             tname = "year",
             idname = "plant_id",
             gname = "adopt_year",
             data = dt,
             panel = TRUE,
             control_group = "notyettreated")
agg_effects <- aggte(cs, type = "group")

# 7. Robustness: Drop Delaware
dt_nodel <- dt[state_inc != "DE"]
feols_del <- feols(lwage ~ treat | plant_id + year,
                   data = dt_nodel, cluster = ~state_inc + firm_id)
summary(feols_del)
```

------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results (Priors)  

The classic managerial “empire-building” view predicts:  
• Higher employment, more plants, higher cap-ex, larger total assets.  
• Lower profitability and productivity because resources are deployed inefficiently.  
• Worker wages could rise if managers share rents to buy labor peace.  

Magnitude guess: Average treated firm increases employment by ≈3–5%, cap-ex by ≈4%, while ROA falls by ≈0.5 pp over five years post-law.  

------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)  

C1. Parallel pre-trends visually and statistically confirmed: 1  
C2. No anticipatory effects (lead coefficients ≈0): 0.8  
C3. Correct treatment/control definition and no spillovers: 0.9  
C4. Robust inference to heterogeneous timing (SA, CS estimators): 1  
C5. No differential attrition or composition change: 0.7  

Average score ≈ 0.88 → credible but still requires careful robustness.
